events.label: Sanga-Sanga SGS / TWT
events.scope: The specific historical interpretation of the linked existing lead; no whole-city or whole-code history is certified.

physicalIdentity.conclusion: One airfield at Bongao, Tawi-Tawi throughout; the pinned 0.0 km coordinate edit is a precision change, and the later 2022 latitude edit is a directory correction, not a relocation.

iata.conclusion: SGS was the reference-directory code in 2009 and is marked obsolete in favour of TWT; airline systems used TWT by 2014-02-09 and today. No IATA record proves SGS was ever officially allocated or dates the change.

icao.conclusion: RPMN appears consistently in every source inspected; no change observed. Not independently verified against the Philippine AIP in this review.

historicalBoundary.conclusion: Only bounds are available: SGS in reference use in 2009, TWT in airline use by 2014-02-09. The 2018-01-01 directory edit and 2019 export are lagging source events, not the code-effective date. An uncited "end of 2011" claim is not admitted.

historicalNames.conclusion: Sanga-Sanga Airport, also called Tawi-Tawi Airport; no formal rename established.

closureAndReplacement.conclusion: No closure or replacement; scheduled service continues under TWT.

continuityInference.note: No interval is admitted. Treating SGS→TWT as continuous across the 2009–2014 window would be a continuity inference with no dated boundary.

evidenceGaps: Official SGS allocation (if any) and the actual TWT effective date are missing; only a 2009–2014 window is bounded by reference/airline observations.
events.nextAction: Seek dated IATA code-directory or airline/GDS notices (Cebu Pacific, Airphil Express 2010–2013) and CAAP AIP for RPMN; do not admit TWT from 2014 by continuity.

sourceObservation.semantics: Pinned directory revision; observing commit time is not an effective event boundary.

directlyEstablishedFacts.fact: PAL Express listed Tawi-Tawi as TWT on its 2014-02-09 archived booking page.

events.label: Duqm DQM / Ja’aluni JNJ
events.scope: The specific historical interpretation of the linked existing lead; no whole-city or whole-code history is certified.

physicalIdentity.conclusion: Duqm (OODQ) and Ja’aluni (OOJA) are separate aerodromes in the national AIP; the pinned record is the Duqm site (0.9 km coordinate refinement), and the "Duqm Jaaluni" before-label conflates it with the inland Ja’aluni strip about 35 km west.

iata.conclusion: DQM is used for the Duqm airport; JNJ is attributed only by directories and a 2013 business report that already conflates the two places. No IATA allocation of JNJ, to any site, was found.

icao.conclusion: OODQ and OOJA are distinct AIP aerodrome indicators; OOJA AIP pages carry 2014-05-29 dates. First allocation dates are not held.

historicalBoundary.conclusion: Duqm opened and Oman Air service started 2014-07-23; this is an opening/service date, not a DQM allocation boundary. The JNJ→DQM directory edits (2015–2018) are not historical boundaries.

historicalNames.conclusion: "Duqm Jaaluni Airport" is not established as an official name of the Duqm site; AIP and authorities use Duqm.

closureAndReplacement.conclusion: The Muscat air link moved from Ja’aluni to Duqm in 2014; Ja’aluni remains listed in the AIP and is not shown closed.

continuityInference.note: No interval is admitted; continuity across the two physical sites is explicitly rejected.

evidenceGaps: Whether IATA ever issued JNJ (and for which site) and when DQM was issued remain unknown; last Ja’aluni charter date undocumented.
events.exclusionReason: Exclude the implied same-airport JNJ-to-DQM code transfer: the before-row is a directory record that conflated Duqm with the separate Ja’aluni aerodrome, as the editor history and separate AIP indicators show.
events.nextAction: Retain a separate Ja’aluni (OOJA) lead and the DQM allocation question; seek IATA coding directory or 2012–2014 Oman Air timetable before attributing JNJ.

sourceObservation.semantics: Pinned directory revision; observing commit time is not an effective event boundary.

directlyEstablishedFacts.fact: National AIP lists OODQ (Duqm) and OOJA (Ja’aluni) as separate aerodromes.

events.label: New Bight CAT / TBI
events.scope: The specific historical interpretation of the linked existing lead; no whole-city or whole-code history is certified.

physicalIdentity.conclusion: One New Bight aerodrome (MYCB); Arthur’s Town (MYCA) is a separate Cat Island aerodrome. The pinned 0.0 km coordinate edit is precision only.

iata.conclusion: TBI was the working code by February 2006; CAT appears as an island-level "Cat Island" entry listed alongside TBI, and directories later corrected New Bight from CAT to TBI as an incorrect code. CAT was associated with Cascais by 2016. No IATA record of a CAT allocation to New Bight exists in this review.

icao.conclusion: MYCB in the Bahamas CAA register; the directory added it in the same 2018 correction.

historicalBoundary.conclusion: The 2018-04-26 directory correction (and its 2019 derived observations) is not a real-world boundary. No effective date for TBI or for any withdrawal of CAT is held.

historicalNames.conclusion: Register name New Bight; airline usage "The Bight" historically. No rename established.

closureAndReplacement.conclusion: No closure or replacement of New Bight; CAT reuse at Cascais is a separate, unproven-dated question.

continuityInference.note: No interval is admitted; equal coordinates in CAT and TBI rows reflect the same airport, not continuity of either code.

physicalIdentity.conclusion: Two distinct airfields: the old county-town airport (1700 m runway, 1.2 km from the centre) and the relocated Qiemo Yudu airport about 11–12 km north (2800 m runway). The pinned 11 km shift is a real site change, not a correction.

iata.conclusion: IQM attached to the old site in 2010–2012 reference lists and to Yudu now; IQM stayed listed through the 2011–2016 service gap. No IATA or CAAC record documents its reassignment or date.

icao.conclusion: ZWCM attached to the old site in 2012 reference data and to Yudu now; reassignment date not documented (no AIP amendment or NOTAM retrieved).

historicalNames.conclusion: "Yudu" appears in official CAAC use by 2016-09-05; no formal naming decision or date held.

closureAndReplacement.conclusion: Yudu is the relocation (迁建) of the old Qiemo civil airport, approved by Guohan [2012] No. 62; service did not transfer seamlessly because the old site stopped in 2011.

continuityInference.note: No interval is admitted. Assigning IQM to Yudu from 2016-12-19 would rest on continuity inference; it is recorded as a hypothesis only.

evidenceGaps: IQM/ZWCM reassignment record, exact May 2011 closure day and whether IATA marked the code closed in 2011–2016 are missing.
